@graph.description: Search index supply and standing operations for The Flat Rate Movers: the standing measurement system of the Retrieval Machine’s search-index element. One dataset file joins the demand side (the buyer-intent query clusters generated from the estate’s own rubric), the supply side (every page of the estate with its schema types, word count, internal inlinks, per-page JSON digest and indexation state), and the evidence side (sampled standing, Search Console verdicts and the era-tagged pre-rebuild console window), plus the competitor supply observed in the same sampling, the third-party records that corroborate or corrupt the company’s facts, and the named gaps with their designed solutions. Standing is recorded only from evidence that exists: a cluster with no observation carries no standing row, observed absence is recorded as observed absence, and no position, rating or metric is invented or zero-filled anywhere in the file.

@graph.name: How the Search Index Dataset Is Built
@graph.description: Method. The generator (scripts/build-search-index.js in the Flat Rate Machine) reads the paths registry for every location and builds all seven tables from the live estate in one run: clusters are grouped mechanically from the rubric database by (service, intent class, geo scope, target URL); URL supply is mined from the registries, the source shell, the served head data and the per-page JSON files; standing observations are admitted only from evidence on file — the research dossier’s dated live sampling and the Search Console verdicts — and the generator rejects any observation missing its method, era or source; the console window is joined from the rubric’s era-tagged evidence tables without aggregation or zero-filling; competitor, third-party and gap records are transcribed from the research dossiers with their check dates, under a schema bar the generator enforces in code. The url_supply digest is the SHA-256 of the page’s per-page JSON file in the public tree at generation time; a completed batch seals exactly those bytes, and the verification suite asserts the supply digests equal the served signed index after every batch. The file’s dateModified is the estate lastmod-ledger date for this file’s URL, wired by the seal (Batch Q124, 2026-11-03) — outside a seal the generator falls back to the newest evidence date among its inputs — never the wall clock, so regeneration is byte-stable and checkable. Update cadence: the dataset regenerates in every estate batch that changes pages, rubric rows or standing evidence, and reseals in the same motion.

@graph.name: Search Index Dataset Sources
@graph.description: Sources, with their dates and eras kept distinct. (1) The estate’s own registries and rubric database — the demand and supply truth, current at generation. (2) Live search sampling of 2026-10-31 (Retrieval Machine Dossier 01 §§2–3): sampled positions and pack orders, labeled [OBS] in the dossier, post-rebuild era, small-sample by design and never blended with console data. (3) Search Console URL-inspection verdicts of 2026-10-31: 11 URLs inspected in the standing indexing pass; the same verdicts were ingested into the rubric outcome-evidence log (161 evidence rows). (4) The Search Console performance export for 2026-07-29 to 2026-10-28: pre-rebuild era evidence, attached to rubric rows by exact normalized text match only where the target page existed in the export and still exists; its totals describe the old site, not this one. (5) Third-party record checks of 2026-10-30 (backlink program wave 1) and 2026-10-31 (Dossier 03 re-verification, with each crawl’s age stated there). No source is presented as fresher than it is.

@graph.name: Search Index Boundaries and Non-Claims
@graph.description: What this dataset never does. It never invents a position, a metric, a rating or a review count — for the company or for any competitor. It never presents the pre-rebuild console window as current performance, and never averages methods together. It never claims a third-party record corrected without direct-fetch proof. It contains no representation of any service the company has not confirmed and published through the normal estate path: the research dossiers’ expansion candidates (after-hours cross-dock work, auction-exit medical logistics, data-center decommissioning’s physical layer, small-count rack moves as a named segment, equipment buyback) appear nowhere in this file and enter only if the owner confirms the capability and the service is published first. Competitor records are benchmark observations about their owners’ supply and feed no company claim. The provenance certificate proves origin and integrity of this file only; it is not a ranking input and is not represented as one.
